what: First idle-box re-baseline of all four performance benchmarks since the frame-deletion era, v96-v100, the cf plumbing and the entry-point decomposition. The claim under test: none of that moved a hot path.
verdict: CLAIM HELD on every benchmark. Two DOC findings, no code regressions.

box.note: No production run on the box. Every figure carries the 1-minute load average at its own measurement; the bridge-throughput arms saturate the box by design, so their start-load is reported rather than treated as contention.

ab_control.why: The leaf's documented primary metric (~3.46k calls/encode) is a NAKED-ENCODE-era figure and is NOT comparable to the current full-protocol benchmark, so the documented threshold could not be applied. Settled instead with a same-session A/B on an idle box.
ab_control.before_commit: bcdd868 (the frame deletion; everything after it is the change under test)

obs_build.verdict: NO REGRESSION. +2.4% calls/encode against a 10% threshold, and it tracks the +2.6% obs-dim growth almost exactly — more dims written by the same algorithms, no new hot loop. cProfile top-of-list unchanged in structure.

trainer_turn.verdict: NO REGRESSION from the change under test (0.921 -> 0.899 ms our-CPU, shares flat). The frame deletion itself bought -8% our-CPU (1.001 -> 0.921) and removed the 0.060 ms turn-history line.
trainer_turn.doc_finding: The baseline documented in the root CLAUDE.md (obs build ~88% of our CPU, state_encoder.encode ~80%, parse ~7%, reward ~4%) is STALE BY GENERATIONS and does not match ANY of the three arms. Reward has been 23-27% of our controllable CPU for at least three generations, not 4%; process_turn_reward alone is 0.21 ms, the second-largest per-decision consumer. The stale line would misdirect anyone optimizing this path.

workers_48.loadavg_note: residual from the preceding 8-worker arm, decaying; both arms saturate 16 cores by design and the node arm runs first, so if anything this ordering favours node's residual-free window less, not more

bridge_impl_throughput.verdict: NO REGRESSION — reproduces and slightly exceeds the documented ratios (1.195 vs 1.18 at 8; 1.450 vs 1.41 at 48). Both impls faster in absolute than the documented figures; child RSS matches exactly (223/9 MB at 48).

bridge_heap_growth.banner_note: A first attempt DID carry the busy banner (load 33, residual from the 48-worker throughput arm). It was discarded and re-run clean per the docs' own rule rather than recorded with a caveat.
bridge_heap_growth.impl: node (attach_bridge_transport default — matches the documented node baseline)
bridge_heap_growth.verdict: NO REGRESSION — textbook match to the documented profile (189.8 -> 229.3 MB, +0.16 MB/1k battles steady state). The 2521 battles played exceed the ~2137 a child sees in a 3h launcher window, so the 'no recycle needed under the launcher' conclusion is re-confirmed on the actual production horizon.

doc_findings.finding: The stated PRIMARY regression metric, '~3.46k calls/encode, >10% above is a regression', is a naked-encode-era figure. The benchmark has threaded the full env protocol since 2026-08-16 and now measures ~5.43k. Applying the documented rule mechanically would declare a false +57% regression. The leaf also carries a stale 'obs 2437' parenthetical; the encoder measures 2501.
doc_findings.severity: would mislead the next reader running the mandatory gate

doc_findings.finding: 'obs build ~88% of our CPU (state_encoder.encode ~80%), parse ~7%, reward ~4%' matches no arm measured today. Actual: obs 63%, reward 27%, parse 9%. Reward has been ~23-27% for at least three generations.
doc_findings.severity: would misdirect optimization effort away from the second-largest consumer
